blocks.text: Buying a Condo Under $800,000 in Maple Ridge, BC

parts.t: With a budget under $800,000, condo buyers in Maple Ridge can choose from nearly the entire local apartment market—from entry-level one-bedroom units in the $380,000–$480,000 range to modern two-bedroom, two-bathroom corner suites and top-floor penthouses between $525,000 and $775,000. Over half of all housing in East Central Maple Ridge (52.7%) consists of apartment buildings clustered within walking distance of Haney Place Mall, Memorial Peace Park, and Port Haney West Coast Express Station.

Recent and established wood-frame and mid-rise buildings along 223 St, 224 St, 227 St, Brown Ave, Selkirk Ave, and Dewdney Trunk Road give buyers walkable access to grocery stores, the Maple Ridge Leisure Centre, and rapid R3 Lougheed Hwy Express bus service to Coquitlam Central SkyTrain Station.

What can I buy for under $800,000 in the Maple Ridge condo market?

Under $800,000 covers virtually the entire Maple Ridge condo market, including older 1- and 2-bedroom suites in the $380,000–$500,000 bracket and newer 2-bedroom + den and 3-bedroom apartments built since 2018 in the $550,000–$780,000 range.
Which Maple Ridge condos are walkable to the West Coast Express?

Buildings in southern East Central along River Road, 223 Street, 224 Street, and Callaghan Avenue sit within walking distance of Port Haney West Coast Express Station, while buildings near Dunn Avenue in Southwest Maple Ridge are closest to Maple Meadows Station.
What do monthly strata fees cover in Maple Ridge condo buildings?

Monthly strata maintenance fees typically cover building insurance, professional management, landscaping, garbage/recycling, elevator maintenance, and contributions to the Contingency Reserve Fund (CRF); some buildings also include hot water or gas.
Are pets and rentals allowed in Maple Ridge strata condos?

Under British Columbia's Strata Property Act amendments, strata corporations can no longer enforce general rental-restriction bylaws (though short-term Airbnb-style rentals can still be banned). Pet bylaws vary by building—typically allowing one or two dogs or cats, sometimes with height or weight limits.
Why is the strata insurance deductible important when buying a condo?

In BC, if a water leak or fire originates in a strata lot, the strata corporation can seek to recover the water-damage insurance deductible (often $25,000 to $100,000) from the owner. Always verify the current insurance certificate so your condo homeowner policy covers the full deductible.
